qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Unassailable regulatory and reputational duopoly in credit ratings with Moody's, where regulatory mandates (NRSRO) and institutional investment guidelines require dual ratings to issue debt. S&P Dow Jones Indices owns the preeminent equity benchmark (S&P 500) with unmatched liquidity network effects. Proprietary commodity benchmarks (Platts) and Market Intelligence create high workflow switching costs. Empirical proof: Operating ROIC >100% across the cycle (negligible tangible capital required), operating margins ~45-50%, and continuous contractual 3-5% price hikes with near-zero churn. Primary erosion threats: periodic cyclical debt issuance freezes (e.g. 2022-2023 rate shocks), regulatory scrutiny of rating agency fees, and rapid expansion of private credit bypassing traditional public ratings.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Unassailable global toll booth spanning credit ratings, benchmark equity indices, and mission-critical financial data. Operating ROIC exceeds 100% on tangible capital, free cash flow conversion averages 114%, and interest coverage is pristine at >22x with net debt repayable in ~2.4 years of net income. Structurally insulated across all 5 macrotrends due to regulatory mandates, nominal debt growth matching inflation, and proprietary workflow data. qualitative.evidence: S&P Global commands an entrenched global credit rating duopoly alongside Moody's, rating the vast majority of global corporate and sovereign debt. S&P Dow Jones Indices licenses the S&P 500 benchmark, capturing basis points on trillions in passive ETF AUM and trading volume. Operating ROIC has maintained >100% across the decade, with GAAP ROIC normalizing to 11.85% in FY2025 as post-IHS Markit intangible assets amortize. Multi-year FCF conversion is exceptional at 114.25% (FY2025 OCF $5,651M vs Capex $195M, generating $5,220M in Owner FCF on $4,471M Net Income). Balance sheet is conservative with $12.37B LT debt against $1.75B cash (Net Debt / NI = 2.38x) and EBIT interest coverage of 22.57x ($6,478M EBIT vs $287M interest). Management has executed a disciplined capital allocation strategy under CEO Martina Cheung, returning over 85% of FCF via 50+ years of uninterrupted dividend growth and counter-cyclical buybacks, while proactively pruning non-core assets (e.g. spin-off of Mobility Global and divestment of OSTTRA).
